description: Royal Match-style shell for areas 1-5: home screen, areas list, area task page, level start popup and in-level HUD. The board, pieces, animation, VFX and the 1209 tuned levels are kept exactly as they are. Reference screenshots and the list of what differs from the kit are in docs/royal-match/.

userStories.title: Level HUD: Target and Moves, no score bar
userStories.description: As a player, I want the level HUD to be target plus moves, because Royal Match has no score bar and no star rating inside a level.
acceptanceCriteria: A StoryLevelHud component replaces the kit's score/star bar with three panels: Target (icons + counts) on the left, a portrait slot centre, Moves on the right
The kit's ProgressBarScript object is hidden, not deleted
Target icons come from the level's Target assets; counts update as the target is collected
Moves shows LevelManager.THIS.Limit and updates every move
Matches the layout in docs/royal-match/11-level-hud.jpg
Verify in the Unity Editor: enter Play mode and confirm the change from a Game-view screenshot and from [Story] lines in Logs/Editor.log
Typecheck passes: python3 tools/make_typecheck_csproj.py && dotnet build Story.Typecheck.csproj -v q --nologo reports 0 Error(s)
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
userStories.notes: StoryLevelHud draws the strip as a child of the kit's level canvas, so it inherits the kit's scaling, sort order and visibility. It attaches on LevelManager.OnLevelLoaded/OnStartPlay, not on scene load — LevelManager sets THIS in Start. The kit's score bar, star markers and counters are deactivated; the kit's Targets group is only faded to alpha 0, because TargetsGroup destroys its icons in OnDisable and LevelManager's collect animation flies to them. Those invisible icons are kept on the HUD's own slots so that animation still lands where the player is reading. The kit's pause button moved into the booster row's empty middle slot, which is the only place that draws above this HUD.

userStories.title: SCORE-mode levels get a visible target
userStories.description: As a player, I want SCORE levels to state their objective, because removing the score bar left them with nothing to read.
acceptanceCriteria: For levels whose mode is SCORE, the Target panel shows the star1 pass mark and current Score
A self-test logs the target panel contents for one SCORE level and one non-SCORE level
No level shows an empty Target panel
Verify in the Unity Editor: enter Play mode and confirm the change from a Game-view screenshot and from [Story] lines in Logs/Editor.log

python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
userStories.notes: Every level the kit ships carries a Target.SCORE entry and LevelManager.CheckWinLose requires it done like any other, so the score is a real objective on all 1209 levels and the only one on the 176 MODE 0 levels. The HUD now draws it as a target reading have/need against star1 (clamped at the mark, green when met) instead of a static remaining count; the strip still never uses the word 'score'. StoryLevelHud.ReadLevel(level, score) builds the same model from Resources/Levels/N.txt plus Resources/Targets/LevelN.asset with no board in the scene, which is what the self-test drives and what the level popup (US-004) will reuse. Slot counts got best-fit sizing so '270/300' and '4' both fit. Proven in play mode: level 2 (SCORE) read 270/300 with 14 moves; level 1 (BLOCKS) read 100/100 plus 2. StoryScreenTests.ScoreLevelsShowTheirPassMark checks all 1209 levels for an empty Target panel and finds none.

userStories.title: Level start popup: title and goal
userStories.description: As a player, I want a popup naming the level and its goal before I play it.
acceptanceCriteria: A StoryLevelPopup built from StoryUi.RoyalPanel titled 'Level N'
A Goal section listing each target as icon + count, from the level's Target asset
A large green Play button that starts the level via StoryFlow.LaunchLevel
The close X returns to the previous screen without starting the level
No moves count is shown here - Royal Match does not show one; see docs/royal-match/10-level-start-popup.jpg
Verify in the Unity Editor: enter Play mode and confirm the change from a Game-view screenshot and from [Story] lines in Logs/Editor.log
Typecheck passes: python3 tools/make_typecheck_csproj.py && dotnet build Story.Typecheck.csproj -v q --nologo reports 0 Error(s)
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
userStories.notes: StoryLevelPopup.Open(level, areaId, onClose) builds a RoyalPanel titled 'Level N' over a cream Goal card of icon+count slots and a large green Play. The goal comes from StoryLevelHud.ReadLevel(level, 0) — at score zero every HudTarget.Remaining is the whole of what the level asks for — so the popup and the in-level HUD read the same model and cannot disagree. Play calls StoryFlow.LaunchLevel; the X calls onClose, which the area screen passes as AreaScreen.Open(areaId), so the popup has a way back. StoryLevelPopup.Launcher is the test seam, in the shape of StoryLevelHud.Source. The blue gap under the Goal card is where US-005's booster row goes. This surfaced a RoyalPanel bug: the title was inset 110px on all four sides of a 210px plate, so every panel ever built drew an invisible title; fixed, and the primitives test now asserts the title rect has positive height.

userStories.title: Level start popup: booster row
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see and pick boosters before starting, the way Royal Match does.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Select Boosters:' row of three booster slots under the Goal section
Each slot shows the booster icon and the owned count from StoryFreeGame
A slot with zero owned renders locked rather than blank
Selecting a booster toggles it and the selection is passed into the level
Verify in the Unity Editor: enter Play mode and confirm the change from a Game-view screenshot and from [Story] lines in Logs/Editor.log
Typecheck passes: python3 tools/make_typecheck_csproj.py && dotnet build Story.Typecheck.csproj -v q --nologo reports 0 Error(s)
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
userStories.notes: StoryBoosters owns the row: the three pre-level boosts the kit already has (Stripes, Packages, Colorful_bomb), which LevelManager.SetPreBoosts reads after the board is generated. The popup runs in the map scene where LevelManager.THIS does not exist, so the choice is a static applied on LevelManager.OnLevelLoaded — which ReGenLevel fires before RegenMatches reaches SetPreBoosts — and cleared there, since the no-more-matches regeneration fires that event again. Nothing in LevelManager is edited; three public fields are written from outside exactly as BoostIcon writes them, and the kit spends the booster itself. StoryUi.BoosterSlot draws the tile, the red owned-count badge, the green selected ring and the kit's own locked plate. StoryFreeGame now grants all three and gives one of each on first run: nothing is for sale, so a booster the game never grants would leave its slot locked forever. StoryBoosters.OwnedSource is the counts seam, in the shape of StoryLevelHud.Source. This surfaced a layout bug: the popup's vertical metrics were fixed pixels, which fit the 9:19.5 reference and overlapped on the Editor's 4:3 Game view — the row drew underneath Play while every editor test passed. Vertical placement is now fractions of the panel's content height.

userStories.notes: The area screen is now a RoyalPanel: the area's name on the title plate (best-fit, because 150 area names include ones far longer than 'Throne Room'), an 'Area Progress' CreamCard holding StoryUi.ProgressBar with StoryUi.ChestIcon overhanging its right end, then the task rows and Play. Both numbers are read on every Refresh from StoryProgress.TasksCompletedIn and the area's own task count, never stored. The arc line and the area goal moved out of the panel and onto the artwork above it as outlined captions - Royal Match's card carries only the room name, and the story is the one thing this game has that Royal Match does not. Two layout traps surfaced: a caption anchored below the panel's top edge draws behind it and reads as clipped text, and anything built before AreaSceneView.Attach is a lower sibling than the artwork and vanishes under it - the captions are pushed with SetAsLastSibling after every attach.

userStories.title: Area page: Do It rows with star costs
userStories.description: As a player, I want each repair listed with what it costs, so spending a star is a decision.
acceptanceCriteria: Each task renders as a row: icon, the task's own label, and a green 'Do It' button carrying a star badge with that task's cost
Costs come from the task's stars field in the story JSON
A row the player cannot afford renders disabled rather than hidden
A completed task renders as done and is not clickable
Verify in the Unity Editor: enter Play mode and confirm the change from a Game-view screenshot and from [Story] lines in Logs/Editor.log
Typecheck passes: python3 tools/make_typecheck_csproj.py && dotnet build Story.Typecheck.csproj -v q --nologo reports 0 Error(s)
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
userStories.notes: A row is StoryUi.TaskIcon + the story's label + StoryUi.DoItButton carrying the task's Stars. There is no per-task art and no per-task icon field, so the icon is drawn from RepairWork.Classify(label) - the ten-way classifier the repair cutscene already uses - which covers all 807 tasks with ten glyphs and means a lantern task gets a lantern here and a flame there. StoryArt.TaskIcon(areaId, taskIndex) is checked first and misses silently, so dropping task_012_3.png into Resources/Story/Art replaces a glyph with no code change. Unaffordable and not-yet-your-turn rows are greyed via SetGreenInteractable rather than hidden, which moved the story's repair order out of 'which buttons exist' and into an explicit NextTask guard in OnRepair - onClick.Invoke fires on a non-interactable button. Row rebuilds are now keyed on the area id as well as the task count, because price and icon are baked in at build time. Also added JellyGarden > Story > Preview, a permanent Play-mode hook for opening a screen, so no future iteration needs the TEMP runtime early-returns that kept reaching commits. Trap found: the screen tests are meaningless in Play mode - RepairCutscene.Play only calls back synchronously when !Application.isPlaying, so the last repair never reaches OnAreaFinished and only 'the clue fired on the last repair' fails. The tell is that AreaScreen.Open's '[Story] area screen N' line is itself gated on Application.isPlaying.

userStories.title: Home screen: room and top bar
userStories.description: As a player, I want the home screen to be the room I am restoring.
acceptanceCriteria: A StoryHomeScreen showing the current area's artwork full-bleed behind the UI
StoryUi.TopBar across the top with coins, lives, stars and settings
The artwork reflects how many repairs are done, using the existing StoryArt state resolution
Matches docs/royal-match/01-home-area.jpg
Verify in the Unity Editor: enter Play mode and confirm the change from a Game-view screenshot and from [Story] lines in Logs/Editor.log
Typecheck passes: python3 tools/make_typecheck_csproj.py && dotnet build Story.Typecheck.csproj -v q --nologo reports 0 Error(s)
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
userStories.notes: StoryHomeScreen draws the area's artwork full-bleed with StoryUi.TopBar straight on it, and lays out the empty bands US-009 (buttons) and US-010 (nav) will fill. Full-bleed is AreaSceneView's new covering mode: an AspectRatioFitter in EnvelopeParent, cropped by a RectMask2D on the parent — the letterboxed mode the area screen and the cutscene stage use is unchanged and still the default. AreaSceneView's single static instance became a list, because home and the area screen can show the same room at once and a repair must reveal on both. The room is the same StoryArt layer stack the area screen draws, so there is no second art path. StoryHomeScreen.CurrentRoom declines to sit in a restored area and moves on to the first unlocked one still owing repairs. Two traps: the editor test's IsCovering/Aspect assertions pass over a view that letterboxes, so full-bleed was proven by measuring the painted rect in a Play-mode capture against the centre crop computed from the source jpg; and Play mode cannot be detected from AppleScript (AXMenuItemMarkChar reads 'missing value' either way) — screenshot the toolbar, a blue Play button means playing. A first test run was void for exactly that reason. Also removed a // TEMP hook that had ridden into the US-007 commit and dead-coded StoryPowerupTest.
